pest-control-fumigation-nairobi.areas: Nairobi including Westlands, Kilimani, Lavington, Karen, Kileleshwa, Parklands, Embakasi, Ruaka and Kiambu Road, Kitale, plus other towns and counties on request.

sections.h: Signs you need pest control now
p: Do not wait for a full infestation. Cockroaches seen in daylight usually mean a large hidden population. Small dark spots on mattress seams, rusty stains on sheets and itchy bites in a line point to bed bugs. Gnaw marks, droppings along walls and noises in the ceiling at night point to rodents. Mud tubes on walls and hollow-sounding timber point to termites.

If you manage rental units or a restaurant, one complaint from a tenant or customer is a signal to inspect the whole property, because pests move through shared walls, drains and ceilings. Send us a photo on WhatsApp and we tell you what we think it is before the inspection.

faqs.q: Is fumigation safe for children and pets?
faqs.a: Keep children, pets and fish tanks out of the treated area until the technician says it is safe to return. After that, airing the rooms and wiping the surfaces where food is prepared are the usual steps. The technician explains the exact steps for the product used.

faqs.q: Do you serve restaurants and offices on a regular schedule?
faqs.a: Yes. Restaurants, offices and rental blocks can arrange regular visits so problems are caught early. Tell us the size of the premises and how often you want visits and we quote a schedule.

solar-system-installation-kenya.areas: Nairobi, Kitale and surrounding counties, with installations in other counties scheduled by quote.

sections.h: Why more Kenyan homes and farms choose solar
p: Power cuts, rising prepaid token costs and the cost of running a generator push many households and businesses to look for another source. Solar gives you power from your own roof, and a battery keeps lights, a fridge, a router and a TV on when the grid is off.

Farms use solar for borehole pumps, cold storage, electric fences and lighting, where running a power line is expensive. We size each system around the equipment you actually run, so you do not pay for more than you need.

A solar system is not install and forget. Panels collect dust, especially in dry months and near murram roads. Cable joints loosen over time and batteries age faster when they are discharged too deep. Our maintenance visits cover panel cleaning, connection checks, inverter settings and battery health.
Keep a simple note of how long your lights and appliances run. If the battery goes flat earlier than it used to, tell us. It often means the load has grown or a battery needs attention.

faqs.q: How long do solar panels last?
faqs.a: Good panels work for many years, and brands normally come with warranty papers. Ask for the warranty terms for the brand you buy, and keep the panels clean so they keep giving full output.

faqs.q: Can solar run my fridge and TV at night?
faqs.a: Yes, if the battery and inverter are sized for them. A fridge runs all day, so we count it in the sizing together with your lights, TV and router, and tell you how many hours of backup to expect.

cctv-smart-security-installation-nairobi.areas: Nairobi, Kitale and nearby towns, with other counties handled by quote.

sections.h: Planning a system that works at night
p: Incidents often happen after dark, so the picture at night matters more than the picture at noon. We test every camera after dark and adjust the angle and the lighting so faces and gates are readable, not just shapes.
We also plan for power and internet. A small backup unit keeps the recorder and router running during outages, and a stable connection keeps phone viewing working.

Cameras that record people are covered by Kenya's Data Protection Act, 2019. Put up clear notices that CCTV is in use, point cameras at your own property rather than at neighbours' windows or private areas, and limit who can view or copy the recordings. If your property is large or you record the public, take advice on what the law requires.

faqs.q: How many days of footage can I keep?
faqs.a: It depends on the number of cameras, the picture quality and the size of the recorder's storage disk. Tell us how many days you want and we size the storage to match.

faqs.q: Can I get support after installation?
faqs.a: You get a support contact for questions after handover. For repairs or extra cameras later, message us on WhatsApp and we quote the work.

sections.h: Living room, bedroom, bar and boardroom
p: Each space needs a different setup. In a living room we usually mount at seated eye level and hide the cables so the wall looks clean. In a bedroom a tilting bracket lets you angle the screen toward the bed. In a bar or restaurant, screens go higher and must be seen from several angles, so we choose the bracket and position with that in mind.
Boardrooms and meeting rooms need the screen, the laptop connection and the sound to work together. We set up the cables and test the connection before we leave so meetings start without trouble.

sections.h: What to have ready on the day
p: Have the TV unboxed, the model number to hand and any bracket you bought close by. Clear the area under the wall so we can work, and tell us where the sockets and the decoder will sit. If you want cables hidden inside the wall, say so when booking so we plan the time.

faqs.q: How high should a TV be mounted?
faqs.a: A comfortable height has the centre of the screen near eye level when you are seated. In bars and rooms where people stand, a higher position with a tilting bracket works better.

faqs.q: Can you move a TV that is already mounted?
faqs.a: Yes. We can take a TV off an old bracket and mount it on a new wall. Tell us the screen size and the wall type so the quote is correct.

agrovet-spraying-crop-consultancy-kenya.areas: Nairobi, Kiambu, Machakos, Kajiado, Nakuru, Kitale and other counties by arrangement.

sections.h: What a typical farm visit covers
p: We walk the rows or the greenhouse, look at the leaves, stems, roots and soil, and ask about the planting date, recent rain and what you have already sprayed. That history often explains the problem as much as the plant does.
Then we write down what we found, what we recommend and what it costs. You can take the advice only, or ask us to supply the products and apply them.

sections.h: Safe handling and storage on the farm
p: Chemicals belong in their original labelled containers, in a locked place away from food, feed, children and animals. Wear gloves, a mask, goggles and long clothing when mixing and spraying, and wash your hands and clothes afterwards.

Do not rinse sprayers or empty containers in rivers, dams or near boreholes. Follow the label for how to dispose of empties, and respect the waiting period before harvest so produce is safe to sell and eat.

faqs.q: How soon can I harvest after spraying?
faqs.a: The waiting period is printed on the product label and differs by product and crop. We write it into your spray schedule so you know the earliest safe harvest date.

faqs.q: Do you work with small farms and kitchen gardens?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell us the size of the plot and the crop. Our range starts at KSh 4,500 and we confirm the exact figure after the visit.

p: Act early. A fridge that is warm inside, ices up or runs without stopping, a washing machine that leaks, shakes hard or leaves water in the drum, and a microwave that sparks or stops heating are all signs to stop using the appliance and call a technician. Running a faulty appliance can turn a small repair into a big one.
Strange smells, breakers that trip when the appliance starts and loud grinding noises also deserve a check.

Leave a small gap behind the fridge so air can move, clean the door seals and do not overfill it. Clean the washing machine filter and run an empty hot cycle now and then. Keep microwaves clean inside and never run them empty. A voltage guard helps protect appliances where the power supply is unstable.

faqs.q: How long does an appliance repair take?
faqs.a: Simple faults can often be fixed during the visit. If a part has to be sourced, we tell you the likely timing in the quote before you decide.

faqs.q: What should I do before the technician arrives?
faqs.a: Switch the appliance off, note what it was doing when it failed and any error code, and clear space around it. A short video sent on WhatsApp helps us prepare.

p: Landlords usually inspect a house before returning a deposit, so a thorough move-out clean helps you avoid disputes. We scrub kitchens, bathrooms, floors and the surfaces where dirt shows in the final check. Tell us which areas your landlord cares about most.
Short-stay hosts need fast, repeatable cleans between guests, and offices need floors and carpets refreshed with little disruption. We plan the team size around your deadline.

After building or renovation work, we remove cement dust, paint splashes and debris that ordinary cleaning cannot lift. Tell us the size of the space and how dusty it is, and send photos if you can, so our quote fits the job.

sections.h: How to prepare for the team
p: Move small valuables and fragile items to a safe place, clear the surfaces you want cleaned and tell the team about delicate fabrics or floors. If you want certain areas done first, say so at the start.

faqs.q: Do you bring your own equipment?
faqs.a: Yes. The team uses steam vacuuming, extraction machines and floor scrubbers. If you want a product avoided because of allergies or a sensitive surface, tell us when you book.

faqs.q: Can you add a sofa and mattress to a house clean?
faqs.a: Yes. Sofa extraction and mattress sanitation can be added to a house clean. Tell us how many items so the quote is accurate.

p: Call a technician quickly for burning smells at sockets or the distribution board, sparks, warm or discoloured plugs, shocks from taps or appliances, and water leaking near wiring. Switch off the affected circuit if it is safe to do so and stay clear until it is checked.
For plumbing, a burst pipe, a leak that keeps getting worse or water coming through a ceiling needs the main valve closed first, then a call.

sections.h: Planned maintenance for landlords and managers
p: Routine checks on taps, toilets, water heaters, breakers and sockets catch small faults before they become emergencies, and tenants notice the difference. If you manage several units, tell us how many and we plan visits instead of repeated call-outs.

faqs.q: Do you supply the materials?
faqs.a: Materials are quoted with the job. For water heaters we do both supply-and-fit and fit-only, and we confirm which in your quote.

faqs.q: Can you come after hours or in an emergency?
faqs.a: Message us on WhatsApp with the problem, your location and a photo. We tell you the fastest visit available and whether an after-hours charge applies.

sections.h: Questions to ask before you book
p: Ask what pest the technician expects, what the price includes, how many visits are planned and what happens if the pest returns. Clear answers on all four show that the provider has looked at your problem instead of quoting a flat number.
Ask also how long you must stay out, what to cover or remove, and whether follow-up is included. Get the answers in writing, even if it is only a WhatsApp message.

sections.h: Which pests are most common in Nairobi homes
p: Cockroaches thrive in kitchens, drains and warm bathrooms. Bed bugs spread through luggage, second-hand furniture and shared bedding, which is why short-stay units are often affected. Rodents enter through gaps around pipes and roofs. Termites live in soil and attack timber and sometimes wall plaster. Ants, fleas and flies are usually linked to food waste, pets and drains.

faqs.q: Should I treat when I only see one cockroach?
faqs.a: A single cockroach seen at night may be a visitor, but one seen in daylight, or several in a week, usually means a nest nearby. A quick inspection tells you which it is.

faqs.q: How long before the pests are gone after treatment?
faqs.a: Some pests die within hours, while others need days as baits work through the colony or a second visit finishes the job. Your technician explains what to expect for your pest.

p: Write down three numbers: the watts you need at the same time, the hours you need power, and how many hours of backup you want when the grid is off. Those numbers, with the type of system, set the price. A small system for lights, phone charging and a TV sits near the low end of our range. A home that runs a fridge, a pump and a water heater, or a farm with a borehole, sits much higher.

Do not buy panels first and design later. Do not choose an inverter that is too small for the pump or iron you plan to run, and do not skip earthing and surge protection. Cheap cable and loose joints cause heat and failures. Ask for the equipment brands, specifications and warranty terms in writing.

faqs.q: Will solar work on cloudy or rainy days?
faqs.a: Panels still produce power under cloud, but less than in full sun. A properly sized battery and a hybrid design cover cloudy spells so you are not left without power.

faqs.q: Is solar worth it if I already have Kenya Power?
faqs.a: Often yes when outages are frequent or token costs are high, but it depends on your use. We compare your usage with the system cost before you decide.

p: Camera count, resolution, recorder size, cable length, the type of building and extras such as an electric fence, a smart lock or backup power set the cost. A home with four cameras on a short cable run sits at the lower end of our range. A school, estate or warehouse with many cameras, long cable runs and large storage sits at the upper end.

sections.h: After installation: keeping the system healthy
p: Clean the camera lenses, keep the recorder in a ventilated place and check from time to time that it is recording. Change default passwords and keep the phone app updated. If a camera goes dark or the picture turns grainy, message us so we can check the cable, the power supply and the settings.

faqs.q: Can I add cameras later?
faqs.a: Often yes, if the recorder has free channels and storage. Tell us your plans so we choose a recorder with room to grow.

faqs.q: Is a wireless camera better than a wired one?
faqs.a: Wired cameras are usually steadier because they do not depend on Wi-Fi strength. Wireless cameras suit places where cabling is hard. We advise after seeing the building.

sections.h: Choosing a bracket by TV size
p: Check the screen size, the weight and the VESA pattern, which is the spacing of the mounting holes on the back of the TV, then pick a bracket rated above the weight. Large, heavy screens need a stronger bracket and a wall that can carry the load. Full motion arms put more strain on the wall than fixed brackets.

sections.h: What a good mounting job includes
p: A good job includes checking the wall, drilling in the right places, using the correct plugs, levelling with a spirit level and testing that the bracket holds before the TV goes on. Cables should be tidy and the connectors should not be stretched. We run the TV, the decoder and the sound together before we leave.

faqs.q: Do I need to buy the bracket first?
faqs.a: You can, if you know the size, the weight and the VESA pattern. Otherwise tell us the TV model and we advise on a suitable bracket.

faqs.q: Can I mount a TV above a cooker or a fireplace?
faqs.a: Heat can damage electronics, so avoid a position above a heat source such as a cooker or a working fireplace. We can suggest a safer position.

p: Wear gloves, a mask, goggles and long clothing when you mix and spray. Mix in a ventilated place away from water sources and never use kitchen utensils for chemicals. Keep children, animals and people without protective gear away from the area during spraying.

Write down the date, the product, the dose, the crop block and the weather. This record helps you work out waiting periods before harvest, avoid repeating the same product too often and see what worked. We record what we apply on our jobs, and you can ask us for the details.

faqs.q: What if it rains right after I spray?
faqs.a: Heavy rain soon after spraying can wash off some products. Check the label for any rain-free period, and ask us whether the spray should be repeated.

faqs.q: Where should I store leftover chemicals?
faqs.a: Keep them in the original labelled container, closed tightly, in a locked place away from food, feed, children and animals.

p: How old is the appliance? What is the fault, and is the part available? What does the repair cost against a new unit of similar quality? Has the appliance had repeated repairs? If the answers point to an old appliance with a major fault and a repair price close to a new unit, replacing makes sense. If the appliance is fairly new and the fault is a small part, repair it.

Many faults look alike. A washing machine that does not spin may have a belt, a motor, a control board or simply an unbalanced load. A fridge that does not cool may have a failed fan, a thermostat or a sealed system problem. Paying for the wrong part wastes money, so we diagnose first, then quote.

faqs.q: Is it worth repairing a microwave?
faqs.a: Often the repair price is close to the price of a new basic microwave, so ask for the quote and compare. Never open a microwave yourself.

faqs.q: What spare parts do you use?
faqs.a: Genuine spare parts where they are available. If only a compatible part can be sourced, we tell you before fitting it.

p: Dust ceiling corners, fans and vents, wipe skirting boards and doors, vacuum under beds and sofas, and wash curtains if they are washable. Vacuum mattresses and air the room well.

sections.h: What to do before the cleaners arrive
p: Pack away valuables and small items, empty the fridge if the clean includes it, and tell the team where the water and power are. Point out stains and problem areas at the start so they get attention.

Book professional cleaning when you move in or out, after renovation, before hosting guests, or when carpets and sofas look dull despite regular cleaning. Machines lift dirt that a brush and a bucket cannot reach.

faqs.q: Is the price per room or per house?
faqs.a: It depends on the job. We give a range first and confirm after we know the size, the dirt level and the items to be cleaned.

faqs.q: Can you clean while we are still living in the house?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell us which rooms are in use and we plan the order of work.

p: A rising water bill with no change in use, damp patches or peeling paint, the sound of running water when all taps are closed, and a water meter that keeps moving are all signs. Close all taps, note the meter reading, wait a short time and check again. If it moved, there is a leak.

sections.h: Choosing and installing a water heater
p: Choose a heater whose power rating your wiring can carry. Instant heaters need a dedicated breaker, a cable of the right size and earthing, and the water connections must be sound. Ask the technician to explain the settings and to show you where the isolating switch is.

Know where your main water valve and your main breaker are. Never touch wet sockets or switches, and keep electrical items away from water. If a socket or switch smells of burning, switch off at the main and call an electrician.

faqs.q: How do I know which breaker is for my heater?
faqs.a: The breaker should be labelled. If it is not, ask the technician to label the board when the job is finished.

faqs.q: Should I fix a dripping tap myself?
faqs.a: Changing a tap washer is a simple fix for some people, but a worn tap body or pipe fitting is better left to a plumber to avoid leaks behind the wall.
